retired.note: ADR-0088 D3, the first retirement on MERIT rather than on a date. Its flag-off branch was `Adr0030PlanWorkspace`, a ~257-line second implementation of the plan surface that no shipped bundle could select and that ADR-0080 had already attributed a user-facing defect to. `plan-workspace.tsx` goes 334 lines to 24. The flag-off parity suite (plan-workspace.test.tsx) and the flag-off harness (playwright.workspace.config.ts + e2e-workspace/) are deleted with their subject (ADR-0084 D5); the splitter assertion only that harness carried was PORTED to e2e-toolbar/toolbar.spec.ts, and plan-detail.gating.test.tsx was RE-HOSTED onto the surviving layout rather than deleted — it was pen-gating coverage that merely happened to live there.

$schema-note: enabledSource: "docblock" = the date the flag itself records; "floor" = the earliest date this repository can prove, used for the fourteen flags whose real flip is recorded NOWHERE (ADR-0084). A floor can only make a flag look YOUNGER than it is, so retiring on one is conservative — never premature. It is not corrected by guessing.
sizing:
A batch is sized by BLAST RADIUS. The enablement cohort only sets the EARLIEST date a flag may fall on (enabled + horizonDays); it does not set the batch. Re-spaced 2026-08-09 after the original cohort-only split put 17 flags and ~75 production files into a batch due in nine days — the largest batch on the second-earliest date.
MEASURED per flag: production files referencing the constant, and the number of playwright*.config.ts files that PIN it. The pin count is the one nobody had: VITE_CANVAS_AUTHORING is pinned in 14 configs and VITE_SCHEDULING_MODES in 13, and CI proved a single pinned config costs six specs to convert, not a line.
ESTIMATED, and labelled as such: weight = files + 3x pins and a cap of 45 per batch. The cadence was fortnightly and is WEEKLY from batch-2 (product owner, 2026-08-09), which finishes the queue 2026-12-01 rather than 2027-03-23. Note what that does to the estimate: the batch COMPOSITION was fitted against a fortnight and now has a week, so the cap is the part now under test — halving the cadence doubles the rate of work without re-sizing a single batch. The weighting, the cap and the cadence all come from ONE completed retirement, so they are a hypothesis rather than a plan. `check:flags` tests it for us — if batch 2 takes longer than its week, the next batch date fails and forces a re-fit against a second data point. Re-fit it then; do not defend it.

classA.VITE_ACTIVITY_EDITOR_TABS: Selects <ActivityEditorDialog> or the legacy ActivityFormDialog/Progress/Steps trio. Arguably the worst case in the estate: at least nine unrelated features have had to add a case to BOTH to keep them byte-identical. Missed by the ADR author AND the architecture review; found by the test review reading the code.
classA.VITE_CALENDAR_SHIFT_EDITOR: Selects <WeeklyShiftEditor> + the hours-per-day section, or the legacy weekday checkboxes — two implementations of "author a working week" (ADR-0067).
classA.VITE_CANVAS_WORKSPACE: Selects <PlanWorkspace> or <LegacyPlanLayout>, the pre-ADR-0030 stacked plan-detail page. Harnessed by seven configs — the largest conversion cost in the estate, and the register carried NO note for it until ADR-0088 D5.
classA.VITE_LIBRARY_SCOPING: Selects <Combobox> or <Select> in FOUR pickers (activity calendar, plan calendar, activity resources, resource form). One drift risk repeated four times (ADR-0053 M6).

$classA-note: ADR-0088 D2/D3. Authoritative — `scripts/detect-alternative-surfaces.mjs` is a TRIPWIRE that asserts `detected subset-of classA`, never the converse, because it can only under-detect (a flag branching by early return, by `const B = FLAG ? X : Y`, or through an indirection is invisible to it and is legitimately curated by hand). `classACap` is the MEASURED count and ratchets DOWN after each retirement; raising it needs an ADR.
